answer.rationale:
The loudest signal is the competitor's entry pricing, and memory_73 makes promotional pricing the tempting reflex. But that memory is explicitly a four-week readout on the standard SMB segment with the usual reporting cadence — a window far too short to observe the thing that actually matters here: whether discount-acquired SMB accounts retain and expand, or churn out and depress qualified revenue per account. Acquisition-and-revenue lift measured at four weeks is exactly the shape a discount cohort produces before the retention cost lands. Committing the single non-carrying slot to price cuts against a permanently repriced competitor also risks a margin race we cannot win, so I want the source record before touching it. I therefore verify memory_73 first, primarily to disconfirm rather than confirm.

Second, the two symptoms with real internal causal traction are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), which are plausibly the same funnel breaking rather than two independent problems. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value across self-serve) is the closest match to the failing mechanism, and memory_31 and memory_91 point the same direction. So I verify memory_86 second, checking specifically whether the lift was measured on completion alone or persisted into retained, revenue-bearing accounts. That is the known weakness of this whole memory cluster: 31, 86, and 91 all report proximal funnel metrics — activation, completion, week-one engagement — and none of them report qualified revenue, which is my stated objective. I am not treating them as revenue evidence.

memory_57 (referrals) and memory_44 (enterprise sales-assist) are likely sound but address neither presenting symptom; referrals amplify a funnel that is currently leaking, and enterprise assist ignores the SMB segment under attack.

So: simplify_onboarding, at standard experiment scale rather than broad rollout, because the inherited evidence supports the direction but not the magnitude or the durability. Instrumented on downstream qualified revenue and retention, not just completion rate, so this run repairs the gap in the inherited record instead of inheriting it again. If memory_73's archive unexpectedly shows retention held past the four weeks, promotional pricing becomes a live contender for the next slot — but I will not spend this one on it unverified.
